perfect tense noun

classical

Quint. 1.6.26: cujus praeteritum perfectum et ulterius nōn invenītur
Traupman 226, 248

praeteritum perfectum

the perfect tense

The completed past: lēgī, I read, have read (Traupman 226). Also tempus praeteritum perfectum (Traupman 248); in the perfect tense, tempore praeteritō perfectō (229).

Examples

  • quod verbīs etiam accidit ut illī ferō, cujus praeteritum perfectum et ulterius nōn invenītur

    which happens to verbs too, as to ferō, whose perfect and the tenses beyond it are not foundQuint. 1.6.26

  • Dīc praeteritum perfectum. — Cecinī.

    Give the perfect. — Cecinī.Traupman 241

See also tense, past tense, imperfect tense, pluperfect tense, have.
